newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady, overnight seen softer.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady, overnight seen softer.

text.p: Interbank rates were steady on Friday as the market remained short of funds, dealers said.
But the overnight rate was expected to ease slightly due to maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Friday, they said.
"The overnight should come off a bit, maybe to just below eight percent," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
The overnight traded between 8.0 and 8.8 percent on Thursday.
One-week money was steady at 8.70/80 percent.
One-month money at 8.60/70 percent and three-month at 8.30/50 percent, were also unchanged.
Dealers said there was no sign of Bank Negara lending this morning.
The central bank has been injecting fresh funds into the market for the past two weeks to help eased the market.
Recent heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank to defend the currency from speculative attack had caused a liquidity squeeze.
But despite the central bank lending, the market was too short to prevent a spike up in rates, dealers said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange rebounded on expectations of a softening in interbank rates. At 0330 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered
Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up seven points to 92.25, or an implied yield of 7.75 percent.
The December contract rose eight to 92.54, or 7.46 percent while March 1998 was up seven to 92.63, or 7.37 percent.
